_metadata.description: Soil Health Card (SHC) parameter interpretation thresholds for India
sources: Government of India Soil Health Card Scheme — Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research) soil fertility rating guidelines
TNAU (Tamil Nadu Agricultural University) soil testing and fertilizer recommendation norms
NBSS&LUP (National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning) soil classification
_metadata.extraction_method: DTPA (Diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid) for micronutrients unless specified
_metadata.disclaimer: Critical levels are general guidelines. Actual recommendations depend on soil type, crop variety, and regional calibration. Always refer to your specific Soil Health Card for locality-specific recommendations.

N.name: Available Nitrogen

low.label: Low
low.description: Nitrogen deficiency likely. Crop may show yellowing of older leaves.

medium.label: Medium
medium.description: Adequate nitrogen for most crops. Monitor crop response.

high.label: High
high.description: Good nitrogen status. Reduce N application to avoid imbalance.

N.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines, 2015; TNAU Soil Testing Laboratory norms

P.name: Available Phosphorus
P.extraction_method: Olsen method (NaHCO3 extraction) for neutral/alkaline soils; Bray-1 for acid soils

low.label: Low
low.description: Phosphorus deficiency. Affects root development and early crop growth.

low.label: Low
low.description: Potassium deficiency. Affects grain/fruit quality and disease resistance.

S.name: Available Sulphur

deficient.label: Deficient
deficient.description: Sulphur deficiency. Affects protein synthesis and oilseed quality.

S.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines; Fox & Kamprath (1970) modified for Indian soils

Zn.name: Available Zinc

deficient.label: Deficient
deficient.description: Zinc deficiency. Most widespread micronutrient deficiency in Indian soils.

Zn.notes: Zinc deficiency affects 49% of Indian agricultural soils (ICAR-NBSS&LUP survey)
Zn.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines; Katyal & Sharma, 1980

Fe.name: Available Iron

deficient.label: Deficient
deficient.description: Iron deficiency. Causes chlorosis, particularly in calcareous/alkaline soils.

Fe.notes: Iron deficiency (lime-induced chlorosis) common in alkaline Vertisols of Maharashtra
Fe.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines; Lindsay & Norvell, 1978

deficient.label: Deficient
deficient.description: Copper deficiency. Affects enzyme activity and grain filling.

deficient.label: Deficient
deficient.description: Manganese deficiency. Affects photosynthesis and nitrogen metabolism.

B.name: Available Boron

deficient.label: Deficient
deficient.description: Boron deficiency. Critical for cell wall formation, pollen viability, and fruit set.

B.notes: Boron toxicity possible above 5 ppm; sensitive crops include groundnut, sunflower
B.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines; Berger & Truog, 1939

pH.name: Soil pH

strongly_acidic.label: Strongly Acidic
strongly_acidic.description: Highly acidic. Nutrient availability severely reduced; Al/Mn toxicity possible.

moderately_acidic.label: Moderately Acidic
moderately_acidic.description: Somewhat acidic. Some crops tolerate; liming may help.

neutral.label: Neutral
neutral.description: Optimal range for most crops; maximum nutrient availability.

slightly_alkaline.label: Slightly Alkaline
slightly_alkaline.description: Mildly alkaline. Micronutrient availability may be reduced.

alkaline.label: Alkaline
alkaline.description: Alkaline. Fe, Mn, Zn deficiencies likely. Suitable only for tolerant crops.

strongly_alkaline.label: Strongly Alkaline
strongly_alkaline.description: Very alkaline. Most crops will suffer; requires amendment.

pH.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines; Indian Society of Soil Science classification

EC.name: Electrical Conductivity
EC.extraction_method: EC meter in 1:2 (soil:water) suspension or saturated paste extract

slightly_saline.label: Slightly Saline
slightly_saline.description: Critical for salt-sensitive crops during germination.

moderately_saline.label: Moderately Saline
moderately_saline.description: Critical for growth of sensitive crops; restricts crop selection.

highly_saline.label: Highly Saline
highly_saline.description: Injurious to most crops; only tolerant varieties can be grown.

very_highly_saline.label: Very Highly Saline
very_highly_saline.description: Very few crops can survive; soil reclamation required.

EC.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines; Richards, 1954 (USDA Salinity Lab Handbook 60)

OC.name: Organic Carbon

low.label: Low
low.description: Low organic matter. Poor soil biology and structure; reduced moisture retention.

medium.label: Medium
medium.description: Moderate organic matter. Good management practices recommended.

high.label: High
high.description: Good organic matter status. Supports soil health and nutrient cycling.

OC.notes: OC below 0.5% covers approximately 54% of Indian agricultural soils (ICAR-NBSS&LUP, 2010 survey)
OC.source: ICAR Soil Health Card guidelines; Walkley & Black, 1934

black.description: Heavy, clay-rich, self-mulching soils with high water-holding capacity
black.typical_nutrients: Medium N, Low P, High K

red.description: Well-drained, iron-rich soils; relatively less fertile
red.typical_nutrients: Low N, Low P, Low K

alluvial.description: Fertile, river-deposited soils; good texture and nutrients
alluvial.typical_nutrients: Medium N, Medium P, Medium K
regions: River valleys — Godavari, Krishna, Bhima, Tapi basins

sandy.description: Light, coarse-textured soils with low water and nutrient retention
sandy.typical_nutrients: Low N, Low P, Low K

loam.description: Balanced texture; good water retention and drainage; generally fertile

laterite.description: Highly weathered, hard when dry; reddish-brown; low fertility
